articles.title: Yes to Life, in Spite of Everything: Viktor Frankl’s Lost Lectures on Moving Beyond Optimism and Pessimism to Find the Deepest Source of Meaning
articles.highlight: 一切都取决于个体的人，无论志同道合者多么少；取决于每个人创造性地让生命意义在自身存在中成为现实。
articles.summary: 该文围绕维克多·弗兰克尔的失落讲座，讨论人如何超越乐观与悲观，寻找生命意义的最深来源。文中强调，意义不取决于有多少志同道合者，而取决于每个个体在自己的存在中创造性地实现它。适合想从人本与存在主义角度理解韧性和生命意义的人阅读。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键启示：意义感的根基不在外部认同或情绪取向，而在每个人是否主动、创造性地把生命意义落实到自己身上。
articles.sourceExcerpt: "Everything depends on the individual human being, regardless of how small a number of like-minded people there is... creatively making the meaning of life a reality in his or her own being."

articles.highlight: 跨被试神经表征研究提出，对齐可去除标识信息，却留下同余不变的关系鸿沟。
articles.summary: 该论文关注跨被试神经表征中的对齐问题，题名表明现有对齐可能只完成去标识化，而未实现真正的对齐。其提出的同余不变关系鸿沟为审视跨被试表征对齐的有效性提供了一个待验证的问题视角。
articles.failureAnalysis: 提供的源文本主要是题名、作者与机构信息，缺少摘要、方法和实验细节，因此无法核验该关系鸿沟的具体定义与实证支持。
articles.sourceExcerpt: Journal of Machine Learning Research 1–23, 2026 Symmetry and Geometry in Neural Representations Alignment De-Identifies Without Aligning: A Congruence-Invariant Relational Gap in Cross-Subject Neural Representations Anna Notaroanna.notaro@student.uni-tuebingen.de University of T¨ ubingen, T¨ ubingen, Germany Konrad Zuse School of Excellence in Learning and Intelligent Systems (ELIZA), Germany Letizia Rossatoletro@dtu.dk Sadasivan Puthusserypadysapu@dtu.dk Department of Health Technology, Technical University of Denmark, Kongens Lyngby, Denmark Abstract In brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), inter-subject variability remains a major challenge that limits decoding performance across users. Subject-wise alignment is widely used to improve cross-subject transfer of neural decoders, yet it is typically evaluated only through decoding accuracy, which cannot determine whether aligned representations share greater task-related structure. We therefore distinguish two questions that accuracy conflates: whether alignment removes subject-specific information and whether it makes the rela- tional organization of task conditions more similar across individuals.
